product_from_film: Moe presents a way to see the market value of personal belongings and act on that value.
explains_well: A phone aimed at collectibles leads to a named card and visible price.
unclear: How prices are validated, how selling works and what No Listings means are not demonstrated.
scenario: Recognize a collectible with a phone, see a market value and consider a selling action.
product_clear_basis: A phone scan at 39–40s is followed by a named Pikachu card and $2,750 value at 41–42s; earlier portfolio screens alone are ambiguous.

scenes.action: Black changes to a historical market painting with large years. City views, rolling years and banknote detail carry stock-market and value text, then green HOLD, OWN ASSETS and INVEST cards.
scenes.design: Bold compressed type, currency engraving and neon green.
scenes.purpose: Frame personal value through familiar financial language.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 0–14s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Torn photo stacks show financial/property references. Old-computer footage with chat bubbles asks about wealth; records, shoes and furniture appear with circular price-like labels.
scenes.design: Paper tears, archival-looking screens and isolated object cutouts.
scenes.purpose: Broaden assets from finance to owned things.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 14–28s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A reel recorder, people and a room accompany bought/kept/forgotten text. A falling chart over a banknote changes to a phone portfolio with a rising green graph; a green monitor text card follows.
scenes.design: Retro media, bold white copy, phone dashboard and green CRT treatment.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 28–39s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A person points a phone at items on a bed. A Pikachu collectible card with $2,750 appears over the scene, then alone. Marketplace-like source cards and up-to-the-minute-data text follow.
scenes.design: Warm room footage, black valuation card, green price and dark data grid.
scenes.purpose: Make scanning and market valuation tangible.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 39–47s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A List Item button sits across marketplace-name strips. NO LISTINGS text and a bargaining chat follow, then old computer users, city and a boombox.
scenes.design: Lime button and typography; small blue/white chat bubbles.
scenes.purpose: Suggest a different selling experience, though the actual mechanism is unclear.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 47–57s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A held phone appears before WELCOME TO THE MARKET OF EVERYTHING, then the Moe mark rests on black.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 57–60.84s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

categories.finding: Financial history broadens to possessions, then a portfolio, scan/value example and selling claim.
0s is black; a large 1790 then 1792 overlays a historical market scene. It signals a history story rather than a present user task.
People who own collectibles or unused goods are implied. The scan-to-price task becomes clear at 41–42s, late in the film.
Photo stacks, circular object labels, phone scale changes and floating price cards give motion-led emphasis. Exact movement paths are not resolved.
The film repeatedly switches between archival-looking footage and black/green text cards. The selected collectible carries continuity through the most concrete demo.
Torn paper, engraving, CRT textures and bright green finance-style graphics combine old and new markets.
Large headlines are easy to identify in sheets. Circular object labels and bargaining chat are small; NO LISTINGS seems to require explanation after List Item.
The inspected ASR draft provides partial script-role support; recognition limits are recorded in A02. Audible voice characteristics and delivery remain unchecked.
categories.reason: Local draft text was read; no direct listening.

categories.finding: Historical-looking images, room/phone scenes and collectible cutouts are mixed. Source provenance and licenses are unknown.

categories.finding: The phone-to-price step is clear silently. The financial-history argument and listing model are less clear without speech.
The centered collectible price card becomes the main focal object. Earlier many type and footage changes compete for attention.
Almost two-thirds of the runtime precedes the scan example. Financial-history references add many ideas before the core action.
categories.experiment: Open with the bed scan and price card, then give one sentence of context.

categories.finding: The stock-market framing pays off in a portfolio of personal items. The final market-of-everything line closes that analogy, but selling is not resolved.
The shift from forgotten belongings to a rising portfolio suggests discovery and opportunity. No actual user gain or response is established.
categories.reason: Emotional interpretation and implied benefit only.

categories.finding: The collectible remains traceable through scan and valuation. The larger montage switches objects frequently and does not finish a sale for that item.
A phone scan and price overlay are shown. Price accuracy, freshness and sale execution remain claims without independent validation.
Lime color and rising-arrow-like Moe lettering support market identity; collectible objects give the product more specificity than banknote imagery.
The scan result is essential. Several history and computer inserts could be removed to explain the selling action more clearly.
For Tin, use the same physical product from phone capture through a generated product card to a final campaign preview.
categories.experiment: Keep one product name and image fixed across every output state.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Show the physical collectible and its matching digital result together before isolating the result.
try: For Tin product capture, point a phone at one product, reveal its extracted card over the same shot, then use that card in a campaign.
Cut a 15-second version with scan, named result, source evidence and one explicit action, using four matched states.
lessons.avoid: Delaying the core scan for a long market-history montage or leaving conflicting listing language unexplained.
lessons.open: Valuation accuracy, selling behavior, audio, exact transitions and source provenance remain unverified.
